title: Webhooks and integration with ticketing systems

videos.script: A link goes down at three in the morning. By the time anyone looks, there should already be a ticket, with the router, the interface and the time in it. {{ticket}} That is what webhooks are for. When something happens, the router makes one HTTP request to an address you gave it, with the event in the body. {{webhook}} In this lesson you write the receiver, a small web server in Python. You subscribe it to a router, take a link down, and watch the event arrive. {{receiver}} Then the parts that make it safe. A signature, so a forged request is refused. A delivery id, so an event sent twice is acted on once. {{safe}} And retries: what the router does when nobody answers, and what is lost when it gives up. {{retries}} At the end, the receiver opens a ticket on the lab's service desk when the link goes down, and resolves it when the link comes back. One incident, one ticket. {{desk}}
